name: Note-Taking
description: Writing thoughts, ideas, or information down to externalize them from your mind and create a persistent reference.

name: Mind Mapping
description: Creating a visual diagram of ideas and their connections, branching from a central concept outward.

name: Space Decluttering
description: Physically organizing your environment to reduce visual and cognitive noise, creating clarity through order.

name: Planning
description: Breaking a goal into sequential, concrete steps before beginning execution.

name: Goal Definition
description: Stating the objective precisely and specifically before beginning — what exactly needs to be achieved.

name: First Step Rule
description: Committing only to beginning — the smallest possible action — without requiring commitment to the whole task.

name: Future Self Projection
description: Imagining your future self looking back at this moment and using their perspective to evaluate current choices.

name: Journaling & Reflection
description: Writing retrospectively about experiences to extract patterns, lessons, and insights from what has happened.

name: Perspective Reversal
description: Deliberately taking the opposing position to understand it genuinely — arguing the other side as if you believe it.

name: Inner Dialogue
description: Splitting yourself into two or more distinct voices and running a conversation between them to resolve internal conflicts.

name: Emotional Reframing
description: Consciously reassigning a different emotional label or meaning to a feeling — e.g., turning fear into excitement, sadness into pleasant melancholy.

name: Sensory Grounding
description: Using the five senses to anchor awareness fully in the present moment, stopping thought spirals by focusing on what is physically real.

name: Analytical Detachment
description: Mentally stepping back to observe a situation from outside your emotional involvement — watching yourself as if from above.

name: Pattern Recognition
description: Identifying recurring structures, sequences, or themes across experiences, data, or behaviors.

name: Brainstorming
description: Generating multiple ideas, options, or solutions without judging them — quantity over quality to open the solution space.

name: Root Cause Analysis
description: Asking 'why' repeatedly until you find the underlying source of a problem rather than its surface symptoms.

name: Two-Minute Rule
description: If a task takes less than two minutes, do it immediately rather than scheduling or deferring it.

name: Task Chunking
description: Breaking a large, overwhelming task into smaller, concrete pieces that are each individually completable.

name: Reward System
description: Attaching a desired reward to the completion of a task, using anticipated pleasure as fuel for doing the work.

name: Friction as Fuel
description: Treating obstacles, resistance, and opposition as motivational energy — converting pushback into drive.

name: Body Dissociation
description: Mentally separating from physical sensations — cold, pain, discomfort — by treating the body as something you observe rather than inhabit.

name: Strategic Planning
description: Long-term planning that treats people, events, and variables as elements to be influenced or arranged toward a desired outcome.

name: Minimal Viable Action
description: Identifying the smallest action that maintains momentum — doing just enough, especially on hard days.

name: Impact Assessment
description: Evaluating whether an action creates real, measurable change — asking 'so what?' to filter high-leverage activities from busy-work.

name: Dream Visualization
description: Vividly imagining a desired future state in concrete detail to build belief, motivation, and clarity about direction.

name: Scenario Forecasting
description: Simulating multiple possible futures to anticipate obstacles, prepare responses, and make better decisions in the present.

name: Self-Acknowledgment
description: Explicitly recognizing and appreciating progress, effort, or growth — pausing to register what has been accomplished.

name: Anti-Behavior Tracking
description: Monitoring unwanted behaviors or patterns to build awareness of how often they occur, as a prerequisite to reducing them.

name: Momentum Building
description: Starting slow and building intensity gradually, gathering psychological energy before delivering a decisive action.

name: Iteration
description: Testing a solution, observing what happens, learning from the result, and adapting — repeating this cycle until something works.
